outcome: The core question — whether a dense set of points in the plane with all pairwise rational distances exists — remains fully unresolved as of September 2026, with no new unconditional or conditional result changing the pre-2024 state of the art (Tao/Shaffaf and Ascher-Braune-Turchet's conditional-on-Bombieri-Lang negative answer, and Solymosi-de Zeeuw's unconditional curve result).
summary: The Erdős–Ulam problem (dense rational-distance point set in the plane) is unchanged since 26 January 2024. Both erdosproblems.com/212 (the maintained Erdős-problem tracker, last edited 16 October 2025 per the triage-independent check) and the current Wikipedia article (fetched directly; most recent citation is Shaffaf 2018) list the problem as open, with progress summaries stopping at the pre-2024 conditional results (Tao 2014 blog / Shaffaf 2018 and Ascher-Braune-Turchet 2019, both showing the Bombieri-Lang/Lang-type conjectures imply a negative answer; Solymosi-de Zeeuw's unconditional finiteness-on-curves result; Pasten's abc-conjecture-conditional result). No new paper, preprint, or announcement dated 2024-2026 addresses the unconditional dense-set question itself. I checked several adjacent papers that could plausibly be mistaken for progress on this problem, and none qualifies as a case or resolution of it: (1) Greenfeld-Iliopoulou-Peluse, 'On integer distance sets' (arXiv:2401.10821, v1 19 Jan 2024 — one day before the window opens; v2 Mar 2024; v3 25 Aug 2025) proves unconditional near-optimal structure/diameter bounds, but for INTEGER distance sets, which must be finite by construction — this is a different problem (finiteness of integer-distance sets, tracked separately as erdosproblems.com #213) from the density question about RATIONAL distances that Erdős-Ulam asks; it is a related problem under §3.1, not a case, since it changes the question (integer vs. rational, finite structure vs. density) rather than restricting it. (2) Corvaja-Turchet-Zannier, 'Rational distances from given rational points in the plane' (arXiv:2403.02030, Mar-Dec 2024; published in Geometriae Dedicata 2025) studies points at rational distance from a small FIXED number of given points, a variant with different hypotheses, not the dense-set question. (3) Qiu's 2026 construction of infinite rational-distance sets in general position in every dimension produces countable, not dense, sets, and does not bear on the topological density question either way. (4) The widely-covered 2026 AI news (OpenAI's May 2026 model-generated disproof of the Erdős unit-distance conjecture, verified by Gowers/Alon/Wood et al. in arXiv:2605.20695; DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus solving nine other Erdős problems) concerns entirely different Erdős problems (the unit-distance conjecture, problem #90, and others), not Erdős-Ulam (#212); I verified directly that neither the OpenAI paper nor the Quanta Magazine survey of the AI-solved-Erdős-problems wave (3 Aug 2026) mentions Erdős-Ulam or rational-distance-set density. No AI system is credited with any contribution to this specific problem. erdosproblems.com does note the problem has been formalized in Lean, but this is a statement formalization with no bearing on a proof and no AI credited for it.
competing_reading: None of the adjacent papers plausibly recodes as a 'case' of Erdős-Ulam under a stricter reading — each changes a hypothesis (integers instead of rationals, fixed anchor points instead of a free dense set, finite construction instead of density) rather than restricting the stated question, so I am confident in classifying all of them as related problems rather than partial progress. The one item worth flagging as a closer call is the integer-distance-sets paper: since a dense rational-distance set would presumably need to avoid the same collinear/concyclic degeneracies the integer paper controls, a reader could argue the structural techniques are 'about' the same phenomenon. But the integer paper's sets are necessarily finite and address a formally distinct Erdős conjecture (unconditional integer version), and it does not change what could be written in the Erdős-Ulam bullet, so I kept it out of scope.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, either resolving Erdős-Ulam unconditionally, proving a case with the free choice of finitely-or-infinitely-many dense points still intact (e.g., a stronger unconditional density bound in the plane), or extending the conditional (Bombieri-Lang) resolution to an unconditional one, together with expert digestion (Tao's blog, a survey, or journal acceptance).
